Interface SlotScreenHook

public interface SlotScreenHook
The neutral plug MenuKit exposes so panel-hosted registered slots can resolve hover/click through a library-owned screen dispatch — without MenuKit ever referencing a registered-slot type (§0042).

Draw and reveal are no longer this hook's concern: a registered slot is a SlotElement on the panel pipeline, which renders it inline and tracks its reveal/inertness as panel properties. This hook is the residual input limb — it answers, for a screen point, which in-menu slot a panel-hosted slot covers, so vanilla's getHoveredSlot routes hover/click to the registered slot rather than the vanilla slot beneath it (and eats clicks that fall in a panel's empty space).

The split

MenuKit owns the dispatch: a set of mixins on AbstractContainerScreen (hover / click / scroll / release) that fire on every container screen — survival inventory, creative (via super.render), and every chest/furnace/anvil. MenuKit-Containers owns the registered-slot input resolution: fed by the live SlotElementRegistry, it answers which MKCSlot (if any) a panel-hosted slot covers at a screen point. That resolution plugs in here. Drawing the slot is the panel pipeline's job (a SlotElement renders inline), not this hook's.

Registration & absence

MenuKit-Containers registers the single implementation once at client init via SlotScreenDispatcher.setHook(SlotScreenHook). When MenuKit-Containers is not loaded (an MK-only consumer), the hook stays null and every dispatch call is a cheap no-op — there are no slots without MenuKit-Containers, so there is nothing to dispatch.

Why a library-owned dispatch at all (the §0019 evolution)

MKCSlots historically shipped no dispatch — the consumer hand-wrote a per-screen render/input mixin and called the static helpers. That left slots silently invisible on any screen the consumer forgot (creative is a sibling class of the survival inventory, not a subclass, so targeting "the inventory screen" missed it). Inventory-screen parity reframes that as a broken library promise: a consumer registers a slot once and the library guarantees it manifests + behaves the same on every inventory-bearing screen it could show on. Panels already work this way (their ScreenPanelRegistry / SlotGroupPanelRegistry are library-owned, consumers register adapters); this gives slots the same.

      Fired at getHoveredSlot HEAD. Returns whether a revealed panel-hosted slot claims the point and which in-menu slot wins it (see SlotHoverResult).

    • mouseClicked

      boolean mouseClicked(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?> screen, double mouseX, double mouseY, int button)
      Fired at mouseClicked HEAD. Eats clicks that land in a revealed panel's empty space (so a carried item can't drop through to the inert vanilla slot behind it). Returns true when the click was consumed (the caller cancels vanilla handling).
